data.narrative:
T1 Energy (formerly FREYR Battery) is a public-stage climate and energy company founded by Tom Einar Jensen that has raised over $1B. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of four same-sector, same-stage companies: QuantumScape ($3.6B), Enovix ($1.0B), Solid Power ($504M), and LanzaTech ($73M).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The four-company median valuation stands at $752M, with a wide dispersion ranging from $73M at the low end (LanzaTech) to $3.6B at the high end (QuantumScape). This breadth reflects meaningful variance in market perception across battery and energy storage technologies at public stages. The peer-median approach, anchored to the exact midpoint of this comparable set, yields an implied valuation of $752M.

The triangulated valuation range is $639M to $865M, centered on $752M. This relatively narrow band reflects the single-method constraint of the available data; additional triangulation approaches (discounted cash flow, revenue multiples, or capex scaling models) are not supported by the provided inputs. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in the comp set itself—a 50x spread from LanzaTech to QuantumScape—which suggests heterogeneous technology risk and commercialization timelines within frontier energy. Investors should weight the median carefully against T1 Energy's specific stage, burn rate, and path to cash flow generation relative to each peer.
